method: Drift after a take is the clock mismatch in parts per million multiplied by the take length: 1,000 ppm (0.1%) over 1,200 seconds is 1.2 seconds. Drift per minute is 60 x ppm / 1,000,000, and the same drift counted in frames uses the chosen timeline rate. Spacing between re-sync marks is the allowed drift in frames divided by (frame rate x mismatch), and the number of marks is the take length divided by that spacing, rounded up; when the drift at the end already fits the allowance, no mid-take marks are reported. The speed correction is 1 + ppm/1,000,000 in one direction and its reciprocal in the other. Presets cover the 48.048 kHz film-sound mismatch and the 23.976/24 and 29.97/30 timebase mismatches, all at 1,000 ppm; custom values are limited to 1-10,000 ppm. Take length is limited to 12 hours and the drift allowance to 0.1-120 frames. Whether sound ends up early or late depends on which clock runs fast, so both correction directions are shown. Everything runs locally with no file access, upload or storage.
